answer: A gale strikes the zenith of a maker's spiral every epoch and the damage runs down the turns, so every turn's capacity must be re-bought each epoch to earn at all. Supply runs the length of the spiral, and the zenith's height counts the maker's heads, so a turn costs one coin for every turn its maker holds. One honest maker pays one coin an epoch; a maker of a thousand heads owes a million coins an epoch, and a fresh purse inherits the spiral's turns.
